NEW pure faces in scripts/fund_avail_face_impact.py: split_first_ok() (a face of REAL first-announce rows only -- fallback rows are DROPPED, never re-dated) + a generic measure() that carries caller labels in its keys + drop_bias(), which reports WHAT a restriction removes rather than just how far the answer moves. RESULT: the date repair is small, the coverage cut is large -- month-end top-decile turnover pit->first is 1.7%/0.5%/0.7%/0.3% (roe/np_yoy/rev_yoy/gpm) but first->first_ok is 43.3%/11.0%/12.1%/14.5%, with rank correlation still 0.978-0.993: the sample shrinks, it does not re-order. WHY: the dropped names rank best -- for roe they are 10.1% of the sample but 38.5% of the top decile (3.2x over-represented; growth factors 1.4-1.5x). Anchors: 2020-12-31 dropped 788 of 10,693 yet 338 of the 1,069-name top decile; 2026-09-30 only 59 dropped and 9 of 1,174. So avail_first_ok is a BIASED face (deletes the high-roe tail) and must not be used for ranking; avail_first stays the ranking face and first_ok is the honesty bound quoted beside it. Inside the disclosure window the restriction is worst (deadline: 8,713 names wide vs 3,923 restricted, jaccard 0.781) -- the two faces are complements, not substitutes. By year the cost fades: roe turnover 0.92 (2013) -> 0.41 (2020) -> 0.12 (2025) -> 0.02 (2026). DEFECT FIXED ON THE WAY: top_set() took k=max(min_k, share*n) with no cap at n, so two IDENTICAL faces on a thin sample read 0.8 turnover (k=10 over 2 names); now capped, selftest leg pins identical-faces-with-thin-sample = 0.0. Published numbers unaffected (k=share*n at 10k names) but any small-universe reuse would have been silently wrong.
